DirectoryEnvelope.description:
Directory-envelope binding: the top-level object written as ``evidence_envelope.json`` at the root of a bundle directory.

The ``subject`` is a free-form dict carrying the case-specific payload
(certification verdict, gateway claims, handoff manifest, ...). Subjects
are themselves schema-tagged via the legacy schema names, so consumers
can route on either ``envelope_kind`` (preferred) or
``subject["schema"]`` (legacy compat).

This binding is OPEN (``additionalProperties: true``, SPEC 3.7: a detached signature covers the whole document), so it MUST NOT be able to rescue a lean-shaped document that the closed ``LeanBundle`` binding rejects: the ``not`` clause makes the two ``oneOf`` arms disjoint by excluding any document that carries a lean seal key (``manifest``, ``sha256sums`` or ``bundle_sha256``). A directory envelope never carries those keys (its integrity list is ``sha256sums_sha256`` over the sibling ``sha256sums.txt``). Without this clause a lean bundle dressed with ``envelope_kind``/``producer``/``sha256sums_sha256`` and an unsigned extra key (e.g. the retired ``host``) would match this arm alone and pass ``oneOf``.

envelope_kind.description: Dispatch case: 'certification' (ADR-012), 'gateway_airgap' (gateway air-gap validation), or 'handoff' (operator export pack).
envelope_kind.title: Envelope Kind

reproducibility.description: Legacy smrforge.reproducibility_block.v1 mirror of ``runtime_identity`` -- kept for one release for backward-compatible readers; will be removed alongside the deprecated schema (ADR-014).
reproducibility.title: Reproducibility

runtime_identity.description: Canonical smrforge.runtime_identity.v1 block (ADR-014). Single source of truth for who/what/where/when produced this envelope.
runtime_identity.title: Runtime Identity

sha256sums_sha256.description: SHA-256 of sha256sums.txt; pins the integrity list.
sha256sums_sha256.title: Sha256Sums Sha256

subject.description: Case-specific payload. Carries its own legacy schema header for downstream consumers that still grep on names like 'smrforge.certification_manifest.v1'.
subject.title: Subject

DirectoryEnvelope.title: DirectoryEnvelope

EnvelopeArtifact.description: Single bundle artifact with SHA-256 digest.
EnvelopeArtifact.title: EnvelopeArtifact

LeanBundle.description: Lean single-JSON binding: the whole envelope in one ``*.bundle.json`` document (the form SMRForge ships from ``smrforge reproduce``). The seal is carried in-line: a per-section ``manifest`` (inputs/result/provenance, each a SHA-256 digest plus its value), a ``sha256sums`` roll-up, and a ``bundle_sha256`` over the sealed digest-list. Redaction withholds a section's ``value`` (keeping its digest) and drops the corresponding readable top-level copy -- ``result`` for a withheld result, ``reproducibility`` for a withheld provenance -- while KEEPING the signature, which still verifies over the unchanged seal. So ``result`` and ``reproducibility`` are required only when the bundle is not redacted (no ``redaction`` block). The top-level key set is CLOSED (``additionalProperties: false``, ADR-040): the Ed25519 signature binds only ``bundle_sha256``, so any key outside ``schema``/``result``/``reproducibility``/``manifest``/``sha256sums``/``bundle_sha256``/``signature`` plus the optional unsigned ``redaction`` (applied after signing; closed and prose-free, ADR-041) and ``timestamp`` (an RFC 3161 token; closed to ``{format, token}``, the token an opaque strict-base64 DER blob, NOT verified by this binding) would ride UNSIGNED on a verifying bundle; a conforming verifier MUST reject it. The former unsigned ``host`` block is retired: the minting runtime is recorded ONLY in the signed ``provenance.toolchain``.

bundle_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the sealed digest-list; the value the signature covers.

redaction.description: Present on a docket-safe redacted derivative (smrforge.evidence_envelope.redaction.v1): names the withheld sections and pins the parent's bundle_sha256 (REQUIRED; MUST equal this bundle's own seal). Its presence relaxes the result/reproducibility requirement, since a withheld section's readable copy is dropped. Unsigned (applied after signing), so its shape is closed and prose-free (ADR-041): a PASS attests that the present sections are the signed original's and the absent sections remain digest-pinned, and says nothing about who withheld them or why.

reproducibility.description: Readable copy of the reproducibility block; MUST agree with manifest.provenance.value. Dropped when provenance is withheld (redaction).

result.description: The result core (smrforge.result.v1 or equivalent). Opaque to this binding beyond being an object. Dropped when the result is withheld (redaction).

timestamp.description: OPTIONAL embedded RFC 3161 trusted-timestamp token, added AFTER signing by a Timestamp Authority (so it cannot live inside the signed manifest). Unsigned by the bundle key. This binding constrains only its shape (ADR-041: exactly {format, token}, the token strict-base64 DER); its cryptographic validity is a SEPARATE RFC 3161 check, and an envelope verifier MUST NOT report the timestamp as verified. Until that step runs the token is an unverified claim of time.

LeanBundle.title: LeanBundle

LeanManifest.description: Per-section seal: each of inputs/result/provenance carries a SHA-256 digest plus (unless redacted) its value. CLOSED: exactly the three sections (SPEC 2.1.2). The seal commits to the three digests only, so a fourth section would ride UNSIGNED on a verifying bundle; a conforming verifier MUST reject it, and so does this schema.

provenance.description: The signed copy of the reproducibility block; its value (when present) MUST be a LeanReproducibility.

LeanManifest.title: LeanManifest

LeanRedaction.description: The unsigned redaction record (smrforge.evidence_envelope.redaction.v1). A machine record of WHICH sealed sections are withheld, nothing else: exactly these three keys, all REQUIRED (ADR-041), so no conclusion, note or other unsigned claim can ride it on a bundle that still verifies. It carries no free-text field: a constant schema, an enum list, and a digest that MUST equal this bundle's own bundle_sha256 (a verifier checks the equality; the schema checks the form). The former `reason` / `caveats` strings are removed from the format. The record is a declaration by whoever derived the copy, not an attestation by the signer.

parent_bundle_sha256.description: The bundle_sha256 of the unredacted parent. The seal is unchanged by redaction, so it MUST equal this bundle's own bundle_sha256; a conforming verifier rejects any other value.

withheld.description: The sealed sections whose value is withheld (their digests stay pinned). Non-empty.

LeanRedaction.title: LeanRedaction

LeanReproducibility.description: The reproducibility contract for a lean bundle. Appears both as the top-level ``reproducibility`` (readable) and as ``manifest.provenance.value`` (signed); the two MUST agree.

data_library.description: The data-library identity actually used, or the literal marker 'unpinned' when none is externally pinned.

data.description: Residual run-scoped signed facts that are neither the standard reproducibility keys nor lineage (e.g. pack_id, temperature). Present only when a card recorded such facts.

data_library_subset.description: OPTIONAL. The exact data-library files this run read, as [relpath, sha256:<64hex>] rows -- the small, verifiable subset a reviewer fetches and byte-checks to reproduce ONE run without staging the whole library. Each digest follows the NORMATIVE digest rule; each row's membership is checked against the published epoch manifest (whose manifest_digest equals data_library_sha256).

data_library_sha256.description: NORMATIVE DIGEST RULE: MUST be a lowercase 'sha256:<64 hex>' digest binding the data actually used; a conforming verifier MUST reject any other value.

lineage.description: Present only on composed results: the ordered chain of capability steps that produced this bundle.

produced_by.description: WHO produced/reproduced the sealed number: 'smrforge-open-engine' when SMRFORGE's own open engine derived it (so `smrforge reproduce` re-derives it), or 'external:<code>' (e.g. 'external:OpenMC-0.15.3', 'external:MCNP6.2') when the result was computed by an out-of-tree engine and merely PACKAGED here. Prevents an externally-supplied number from being read as open-engine-derived.

toolchain.description: The runtime toolchain that minted the bundle, SIGNED (ADR-040). Advisory on the consumer side: a reviewer on a different toolchain is expected and the result core re-derives regardless; certify reports a difference as a note, never a mismatch. Absent only on bundles sealed before the axis existed (v0.13.0).

LeanReproducibility.title: LeanReproducibility

LeanSection.description: One sealed manifest section: a SHA-256 digest plus (unless redacted) the value it seals. CLOSED: exactly ``sha256`` and ``value`` (SPEC 2.1.1). Only ``value`` is under the digest, so any other key in the block (a note, a verdict) would ride UNSIGNED; a conforming verifier MUST reject it, and so does this schema.
LeanSection.title: LeanSection

LeanSha256Sums.description: Roll-up of the three section digests. CLOSED: exactly inputs/result/provenance (SPEC 2.1.2). ``bundle_sha256`` is the digest of this object's canonical form, so an extra key here would break the seal on a genuine bundle and ride unsigned on a forged one; a conforming verifier MUST reject it, and so does this schema.
LeanSha256Sums.title: LeanSha256Sums

LeanSignature.description: Ed25519 signature over bundle_sha256. Optional at the bundle level as a schema matter, but redaction KEEPS it (the seal is unchanged, so the original signature still verifies over a redacted copy); the schema validates its structure, not the signature's cryptographic validity. The block is CLOSED: the seal binds only bundle_sha256, so any other key in this object would ride unsigned (a false-attestation channel). Exactly {alg, public_key, signature, message}; message is the constant 'bundle_sha256' naming what was signed. Origin (demo vs production) is a property of the key the verifier pins, never a field in the bundle.
LeanSignature.title: LeanSignature

LeanSolver.description: The EXTERNAL solver a plugin actually invoked in this run (e.g. OpenMC), as the solver reports ITSELF: ``version`` from its own version attribute, ``build`` from its own build self-report (for OpenMC the version line, git SHA and compile options printed by ``openmc -v``). ``build`` is omitted when the solver reports none. Never populated from a human-typed value. For as-received externally computed results (``produced_by: external:*``) the toolchain describes the packaging runtime and this object is whatever the packaging card declares; the distinction is carried by ``produced_by``.
LeanSolver.title: LeanSolver

LeanTimestamp.description: An embedded RFC 3161 timestamp token: exactly ``{format, token}``, both REQUIRED (ADR-041). ``format`` is the literal ``rfc3161``; ``token`` is the strict-base64 DER TimeStampResp (correct padding, first decoded byte 0x30 = the DER SEQUENCE tag, so the pattern starts ``MI``), capped so a stapled blob cannot ride. The record carries no free-text field; the TSA's identity is inside the token's certificate chain (the former unsigned ``tsa`` string is retired). Shape only: an envelope verifier MUST NOT report the timestamp as verified -- until an RFC 3161 verification step (ASN.1/CMS/X.509 against a pinned TSA CA) runs, the token is an unverified claim of time.
LeanTimestamp.title: LeanTimestamp

LeanToolchain.description: The minting runtime, folded into the SIGNED provenance so it is tamper-evident (ADR-040): interpreter version and implementation, OS family (``platform``), CPU instruction set (``machine``, e.g. ``x86_64`` / ``AMD64`` / ``arm64`` -- with libm, what can move a last-bit float on the pure-Python engine), the immutable OCI digest of the engine image when a containerized runtime declares one, and the external solver's self-report when a plugin invoked one. Producers from v0.14.0 always write ``machine``; it is optional here only so bundles sealed before then validate until re-minted. This is the ONLY record of the minting runtime: the unsigned top-level ``host`` block that used to duplicate it is retired and rejected.

image_digest.description: An immutable OCI image digest reference, ``<ref>@sha256:<64 hex>``; a mutable tag is not a pin and is refused at capture.

LeanToolchain.title: LeanToolchain

description: The 'smrforge.evidence_envelope.v1' format has two serializations under this one schema identity: the directory envelope (a bundle directory whose root holds ``evidence_envelope.json``) and the lean single-JSON bundle (the whole envelope in one ``*.bundle.json`` document, as shipped by ``smrforge reproduce``). A document conforms if it matches exactly one binding; the two are disjoint by their required-field sets (a directory envelope has ``envelope_kind``/``producer``/``sha256sums_sha256``; a lean bundle has ``manifest``/``sha256sums``/``bundle_sha256``), and the directory arm additionally EXCLUDES any document carrying a lean seal key, so the open directory binding can never rescue a lean-shaped document that the closed lean binding rejects.
title: EvidenceEnvelope
